headline: Rate hike fears weigh on the ASX as PLS takes a hit, while GTA VI previews and Middle East tensions dominate the global picture.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS had a rough session today, dropping 2.65%. Lithium sentiment remains choppy — analysts note the global lithium market deficit isn't expected to bite until 2030, which keeps near-term price pressure on miners like Pilbara. The stock is still well off its highs and today's dip reflects broader caution around the commodity.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI had a solid session today, up 1.18%, riding positive AI tailwinds. Apple's new M6 and M5 Ultra chip announcements boosted sentiment across the AI hardware and software space, lifting this ETF's underlying holdings.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: MSFT edged up 0.95% last night, continuing its strong recent run — the stock is up roughly 28% in the past month. News that China's Moonshot AI is in revenue-sharing talks with Microsoft added to bullish AI sentiment around the stock.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: GOOG slipped 1.23% last night. No major company-specific bad news — the market appears to be rotating some AI enthusiasm toward Microsoft, which has been the stronger performer recently. Google is also in the same Moonshot AI revenue-sharing talks, but MSFT got the bigger bump.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS edged up 0.34% today, tracking a mildly positive US market backdrop. The S&P 500 was essentially flat last night, so this small gain is in line with expectations.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO nudged up 0.22% last night. The big news is all around GTA VI — Rockstar broke its silence on recent footage leaks, calling them 'heartbreaking', and hands-on previews from journalists are expected imminently. Long-term, the GTA VI release is the key catalyst for this stock.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE was essentially flat today, up just 0.10%. Emerging markets are holding steady amid Middle East tensions and a slightly firmer AUD. No major catalyst today.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG dipped a modest 0.27% today — a negligible move for a diversified fund. The slight drag likely reflects the softer ASX 200 session today, with rate hike fears weighing on local sentiment. Nothing to worry about here.

watch_today.title: Rate hike now expected in November — what it means for you
watch_today.detail: Both CBA and ANZ economists have shifted their calls, now tipping the RBA to raise interest rates in November after July inflation came in higher than expected. Three of the Big Four banks now see a hike coming. For a long-term investor, this matters because rising rates can weigh on growth stocks and property-linked assets. Keep an eye on how this develops — a hike isn't locked in yet.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — hold despite today's dip
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals fell 2.65% today and is now sitting at a -23.6% loss on your position. However, the long-term lithium story remains intact — analysts are pointing to a genuine market deficit building toward 2030, and lithium prices are reportedly up 92% year-on-year. Today's move looks like broader market noise rather than a structural change. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — hold, AI tailwinds continuing
watch_today.detail: The Global X AI ETF bounced 1.18% today. Apple's M6/M5 Ultra chip launch and continued AI industry momentum are supportive. Your position is still down 13.8% overall, but the structural AI growth theme is very much alive. No reason to sell — if anything, a continued dip would be a chance to top up for the long term.

watch_today.title: MSFT — strong run, hold your position
watch_today.detail: Microsoft is up ~28% over the past month and last night added another 0.95%. Your MSFT position is now up 12% overall. There's genuine AI momentum here — Moonshot AI partnership talks and continued cloud growth are real tailwinds. No need to do anything; just enjoy the ride as a long-term holder.

watch_today.title: GTA VI previews landing soon — watch TTWO
watch_today.detail: Rockstar Games is about to let journalists go hands-on with GTA VI, with previews expected imminently. This is the biggest catalyst for Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) in years. Your TTWO position is barely in the green (+0.55% overall), but a strong preview cycle could be the spark the stock needs. Watch for media coverage over the next few days.

watch_today.title: Gold hitting new highs — good background signal
watch_today.detail: Gold hit US$4,649 last night, up 1.11%, as Middle East tensions continue and investors seek safety. This is a good reminder that global uncertainty is elevated right now. Your diversified holdings (VDHG, VTS) give you some natural buffer against this kind of volatility.

world.summary: The Middle East conflict continues to evolve with significant new developments, the US is fighting a political battle over voting rights, and Qantas is feeling the pain of spiking fuel costs. A busy day globally.

stories.title: US starts returning staff to Middle East missions after Iran war evacuations
stories.why_it_matters: After evacuating diplomatic staff during the US-Iran conflict, America is now cautiously sending personnel back to its embassies and consulates across the Middle East. This signals that the immediate hot phase of that conflict may be cooling, though the region remains tense. For everyday Australians, a more stable Middle East reduces the risk of an oil price spike — crude has actually fallen to around US$81 a barrel, which is a relief for fuel costs and inflation.

stories.title: Houthi strikes threaten to pull Yemen into wider Middle East war
stories.why_it_matters: Yemen's Houthi rebels have been launching strikes that risk dragging the broader region into a wider war, just as tensions from the US-Iran conflict were beginning to ease. The Houthis have previously targeted shipping in the Red Sea, which disrupts global trade routes — including shipments that affect Australian import costs. This is a situation worth watching as it could reignite oil price volatility and supply chain headaches.

stories.title: Trump's push to restrict mail-in voting sparks legal battles across the US
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration is pushing to restrict mail-in voting, arguing it's a source of fraud — a claim not supported by evidence. A federal court has issued an initial order giving the effort some traction, but multiple Democrat-led states have now filed lawsuits to block it. This fight is shaping up as a major flashpoint heading into the next US electoral cycle. Political instability in the US tends to unsettle markets, so it's worth watching how this legal battle unfolds.

stories.title: Qantas profit hit by fuel shock, beloved A380 to be retired
stories.why_it_matters: Qantas has reported its profit has taken a hit from surging fuel costs, a consequence of the elevated oil price environment driven by Middle East tensions. Adding to the nostalgia factor, the airline also announced the retirement of its iconic A380 superjumbo. For Australian travellers, higher fuel costs for airlines typically flow through to pricier airfares — so if you're planning international travel, book early.

stories.title: Global pushback against divisive politics — a broader trend
stories.why_it_matters: The Guardian is reporting a broader global trend of electorates pushing back against extreme and divisive political movements, pointing to recent election results in several countries as evidence. While this is an opinion piece, it reflects a genuine pattern analysts are watching — more centrist or consensus-driven governments tend to produce more stable policy environments, which is generally good for long-term investors in global equities like VDHG and VTS.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a rough session today, dropping nearly 1% as rate hike fears spooked investors after hotter-than-expected inflation data. Last night's US session was essentially flat — the S&P 500 and NASDAQ barely moved. Gold is surging to new highs while oil eased back, and the Aussie dollar is holding firm above 71 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Fell nearly 1% today as markets digest the growing likelihood of an RBA rate hike in November.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Essentially flat last night — the US market is in a holding pattern after a strong recent run.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Barely moved last night. Apple's M6 chip news was positive but not enough to shift the index.

indicators.name: Gold (WTI)
indicators.note: Gold surging to new highs as Middle East tensions keep investors seeking safety assets.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil eased back over 1.5% last night — a small relief for inflation and airline costs.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar ticked higher, which slightly reduces the AUD value of your US stock holdings.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is interest rates — Australia's inflation surprise has pushed three of the four major banks to tip a rate hike, with CBA and ANZ now both calling November as the likely date. There's also a broader debate about whether Australia's federal system is fit for purpose.

stories.title: CBA and ANZ now both tipping a November RBA rate hike
stories.why_it_matters: After July's inflation data came in hotter than expected, CBA economists officially shifted their call — they now expect the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) to raise interest rates in November. ANZ has made the same call, meaning three of Australia's Big Four banks are now tipping a hike. A rate rise means higher mortgage repayments for variable-rate borrowers and makes saving accounts more attractive. It also tends to put downward pressure on growth stocks and property prices. If you have a variable home loan, it's worth checking whether you can lock in a fixed rate.

stories.title: Unexpectedly high July inflation boosts case for a September RBA move too
stories.why_it_matters: The AFR is reporting that July's inflation surprise was strong enough that some economists now think the RBA could even move as soon as September — earlier than the November consensus. Consumer spending data has also come in stronger than expected, further building the case for the RBA to act. The key message: interest rates in Australia are more likely to go up than down in the near term, and the timeline could be sooner than most people thought a week ago.

stories.title: Australia's federal system under the microscope — from GST to gambling
stories.why_it_matters: A piece in The Conversation argues that Australia's federation — the way powers are split between federal and state governments — is increasingly broken. The examples given include ongoing fights over GST distribution between states, the inability to get a national approach to gambling reform, and the slow progress on gun buyback schemes. This is a slower-burn policy debate, but it matters because inefficient federal-state relations make big national reforms harder to achieve, from housing to energy transition.

ai.summary: Apple launched major new chips today, Google dropped a new AI speech model, and Bill Gates has come out publicly criticising the tech industry for downplaying AI risks. A big day for AI hardware and policy news.

stories.title: Apple launches M6 and M5 Ultra chips — a big leap for AI computing
stories.why_it_matters: Apple has officially unveiled its M6 and M5 Ultra chips, claiming a major leap in both general performance and AI processing power. The M5 Ultra is going into the new Mac Studio. In plain English: Apple's computers are getting dramatically faster at running AI tasks locally — meaning things like real-time translation, image generation, and AI assistants can run on your Mac without needing to send data to the cloud. This is great news for GXAI.AX, which holds AI-related companies across the supply chain, and reinforces the long-term AI hardware investment theme.

stories.title: Google Gemini 3.5 launches a new speech-to-text AI model
stories.why_it_matters: Google has released a new speech-to-text model as part of its Gemini 3.5 AI family. In practical terms, this means Google's AI can now convert spoken words to text faster and more accurately than before — useful for voice assistants, meeting transcription, accessibility tools, and real-time translation. This keeps Google competitive in the AI arms race, though it's worth noting MSFT and OpenAI still dominate the headlines. Relevant to your GOOG holding.

stories.title: Bill Gates criticises tech companies for downplaying AI risks
stories.why_it_matters: Bill Gates has publicly called out major tech companies — including the likes of Google and Microsoft — for being too optimistic about AI and not being upfront enough with the public about the risks. While Gates is broadly pro-AI, his comments are a reminder that even tech insiders think the industry is moving faster than the guardrails. For investors, this feeds into the regulatory risk picture — if governments start taking a harder line on AI, it could slow revenue growth for some of your holdings.

stories.title: China's Moonshot AI in talks with Microsoft, Amazon, and Google over revenue sharing
stories.why_it_matters: Moonshot AI, one of China's leading AI startups (known for its Kimi AI chatbot), is reportedly in talks to share revenue with Microsoft, Amazon, and Google in exchange for using their cloud infrastructure. This is notable because it shows Western tech giants are finding ways to benefit from Chinese AI growth even amid geopolitical tensions. Both MSFT and GOOG — which you hold — could generate meaningful new revenue streams if these deals go ahead.

stories.title: The AI influence operations gap — regulators are scrambling to keep up
stories.why_it_matters: A new analysis highlights that AI is now being used to run large-scale influence operations — fake social media campaigns, AI-generated news articles, deepfake videos — and regulators around the world haven't kept pace. There are currently no clear international rules on AI-generated political content. This matters to everyday people because it makes it much harder to know what's real online, and to investors because regulatory crackdowns could hit the AI industry's growth trajectory when they do arrive.

sport.summary: NRL Round 26 kicks off tonight with Broncos vs Storm at Suncorp — a massive local game for Gold Coast fans. AFL finals are also building momentum, with list changes and SuperCoach finals headlines dominating. And the big news from the NRL transfer market is the new Perth Bears franchise making early signings for their 2027 debut.

stories.title: Broncos vs Storm — Round 26 kicks off tonight at Suncorp
stories.why_it_matters: The Broncos host Melbourne Storm tonight at 7:50 pm at Suncorp Stadium — a must-watch for Gold Coast fans. With the finals only weeks away, both clubs have significant ladder positions on the line. Round 26 also features Panthers vs Bulldogs on Friday night and the local Titans hosting the Rabbitohs on Saturday at 3pm at Cbus Super Stadium.

stories.title: Turbo: 'It's the destination that counts now' — Sea Eagles finals mindset
stories.why_it_matters: Manly's Tom Trbojevic (aka Turbo) has come out with a clear finals-or-bust message ahead of Round 26, saying the team is now purely focused on results, not performances. The Sea Eagles host the Dragons on Friday at 6pm in what shapes as a critical finals positioning match. Manly need the win to stay in touch with the top eight.

stories.title: Perth Bears building their 2027 NRL squad — who have they signed?
stories.why_it_matters: The new Perth Bears franchise, set to enter the NRL in 2027, is ramping up their recruitment. CODE Sports has published an early rundown of their signings and projected best 17 — including some notable junior Wallaby crossover talent being poached. The Bears' arrival will shake up the NRL landscape significantly, adding a west coast rivalry and drawing player movement across the competition.

stories.title: AFL: St Kilda delists former top-three pick among three players cut
stories.why_it_matters: St Kilda has cut three players, including a former top-three draft pick, as the club continues its list rebuild ahead of the trade period. While the specific names haven't been confirmed in the article text available, a top-three pick being delisted is significant — it signals the club is moving on from high-investment players who haven't delivered. AFL SuperCoach finals also start this week, with captain picks and wildcard selections dominating fantasy footy discussions.
